slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.brief: Two particles (e.g. electron and proton) accelerated through the same potential difference; compare their de Broglie wavelengths using λ ∝ 1/√(mK).

stem: An $\alpha$ particle and a proton, both initially at rest, are accelerated through the same potential difference. Taking their charges as $+2e$ and $+e$ and their masses as $4m_p$ and $m_p$, respectively, find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths, $\dfrac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p}$.

verdicts.working: For particles accelerated from rest, \(\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}\). Thus \(\lambda_\alpha/\lambda_p=\sqrt{(m_p e)/(4m_p\cdot2e)}=1/\sqrt8\).

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$ 
$\dfrac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_p e}{(4m_p)(2e)}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{8}}$

Independent check: For particles accelerated from rest, \(\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}\). Thus \(\lambda_\alpha/\lambda_p=\sqrt{(m_p e)/(4m_p\cdot2e)}=1/\sqrt8\).
solution:
For a particle accelerated from rest through potential difference $V$, $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$.
$$\frac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\frac{m_p e}{(4m_p)(2e)}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{8}}$$
